scope: Structured explanation follow-up on the same private source, fixed Korean evaluation question and seven previously selected observations. Same cases are reused; do not sum per-model counts into broader coverage. No private identifiers, source, concrete inputs/results or raw model replies are published.
implementation: 3B began from the uncommitted runtime candidate later committed as 49b1a2b. 7B began after that commit. Only explanation schema, guidance, validation and presentation changed; source/question/observations remain the same. Both requests explicitly use a ten-minute generation deadline; earlier baseline deadlines vary, so this is not a controlled speed comparison.

semanticReview.kind: Agent review against unchanged source, fixed evaluation question and native observations; not an independent third-party evaluation.
findings: All seven case numbers are present, but two entries cite nonexistent source-citation indexes. The product correctly rejects the response.
The runtime-check field lists input requirements, including incorrect requirements, instead of describing validation actually performed.
The caller-requirement and summary wrongly require in-range input despite visible clamping.
Boundary-case explanations misidentify supplied out-of-range inputs as in-range inputs.
An empty-input case is misclassified and assigned a different return outcome instead of the earlier native exception.
Singleton handling is mentioned, but duplicate-position conditions are generalized from collection length and are inadequately explained.

semanticReview.kind: Agent review against unchanged source, fixed evaluation question and native observations; not an independent third-party evaluation.
findings: The completed answer passes exact-quote and per-example reference validation, with all seven examples present.
It describes the main behavior, out-of-range handling and empty-input error correctly at a high level.
The input-check and caller-requirement fields repeat the same conditions instead of distinguishing implemented validation from unchecked preconditions.
The range requirement contradicts the visible clamping behavior, and ordering or data-shape requirements are not explained.
The singleton case is assigned an incorrect returned outcome despite the supplied observation.
Both duplicate-position cases are described as errors, contradicting their supplied returned observations; the latter also assumes a condition absent from that input.
Most examples reuse a boundary-operation citation, which does not itself establish the claimed downstream outcome. Existing-reference checks do not prove this semantic relationship.

limitations: Exact source quotes and complete example indexes do not prove semantic correctness.
This is one function and one evaluation question, not all-language or whole-project accuracy.
Original project tests and scientific validity are outside this explanation comparison.
CPU-only cloud-disabled loopback inference uses existing model files and no paid API.
reviewCriteria: Describe the selected function purpose, inputs and returned data without inventing roles.
Distinguish runtime checks actually present from unchecked caller preconditions.
Explain requested boundary outcomes using unchanged source and supplied observations; distinguish returns, exceptions and interpreter limitations.
Answer the fixed question completely without proposing changes.
Evaluate source-quote and example-index validity separately from meaning.
